individual_assessment: The error must be subpolynomial for every epsilon, not merely o(sqrt(x)); finite Sidon constructions or a better constant cannot settle this. No uniform error mechanism.
literal:
For a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, call
$A$ a Sidon set if all pairwise sums of its elements are distinct, i.e. if for all $a_i,
a_j, a_k, a_l \in A$,

$$
a_i + a_j = a_k + a_l \;\Longrightarrow\; \{a_i, a_j\} = \{a_k, a_l\}.
$$

For a real number $x > 0$ let

$$
F(x) = \max\{\, |A \cap [1,x)| \;:\; A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ is a Sidon set} \,\}
$$

be the largest possible number of elements smaller than $x$ in a Sidon set.

Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$,

$$
F(x) = \sqrt{x} + o\!\left(x^{\varepsilon}\right) \qquad (x \to \infty),
$$

that is,
$\lim_{x \to \infty} \left( F(x) - \sqrt{x} \right) x^{-\varepsilon} = 0$ for
each fixed $\varepsilon > 0$.
title: Sidon set problem

Erves and Tepeh proposed the following two conjectures: (1) if $c_{\mathrm{ind}}(G)\ge n/2+2$, then $\gamma_{1,2}(G)\le c_{\mathrm{ind}}(G)$; (2) for every connected cubic graph $G$, $\gamma_{1,2}(G)>c_{\mathrm{ind}}(G)$ if and only if $G$ is a trilobite graph $T_n$.

Let $T$ be a tree of order $n\geq 3$. A set $S\subseteq V(T)$ is a dissociation set if every vertex of the induced subgraph $T[S]$ has degree at most $1$, and it is maximal if it is inclusion-maximal among dissociation sets. Let $\Phi(T)$ denote the number of maximal dissociation sets of $T$. The conjecture asks whether
\[
\max_{\lvert V(T)\rvert=n}\Phi(T)=g(n),
\]
where
\[
g(n)=\begin{cases}
n,&n=3,4,5,6,\\
3^{\frac{n-1}{3}}+\frac{n-1}{3},&n\equiv 1\pmod 3,\ n\geq 7,\\
4\cdot 3^{\frac{n-5}{3}}+n-5,&n\equiv 2\pmod 3,\ n\geq 8,\\
16\cdot 3^{\frac{n-9}{3}}+3n-25,&n\equiv 0\pmod 3,\ n\geq 12,\ n\neq 21,\\
19,&n=9,\\
1349,&n=21.
\end{cases}
\] The associated extremal problem also asks for a characterization of all trees attaining this maximum.
title: Wang et al.’s conjecture on maximal dissociation sets in trees

For every open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, set $F:=\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega$ and, for $0<\alpha\le 1$ and $x\in\Omega$, define $d_\alpha(x):=\inf\{r>0:\operatorname{cap}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})\ge\alpha\operatorname{cap}(B(\mathbf{0},r))\}$. Determine the optimal dependence on $\alpha$ of the least constant $C_n(\alpha)$ such that, for every such $\Omega$ and every $u\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, $\int_\Omega |u(x)|^2/d_\alpha(x)^2\,dx\le C_n(\alpha)\int_\Omega |\nabla u(x)|^2\,dx$. Equivalently, determine the sharp order of $C_n(\alpha)$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$; the claimed resolution is $C_n(\alpha)\asymp_n\alpha^{-2}$.
title: Maz’ya’s Problem 8 on the capacitary-distance Hardy inequality

literal: Let $T$ be the once-punctured torus, let $\mathcal{C}(T)$ denote the set of closed curves on $T$, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be any mapping class group orbit in $\mathcal{C}(T)$. For every word length $n$, determine exactly the number $N_{\mathcal{O}}(n)=\#\{\gamma\in\mathcal{O}:\ell(\gamma)=n\}$, where $\ell(\gamma)$ is the word length used for curves on the once-punctured torus. Chas's conjecture asserts that these orbit-by-orbit counts admit the claimed exact formulas for every orbit and every word length.
title: Chas’s conjecture on exact curve counting

literal: Given a directed graph $G$, vertices $s,t\in V(G)$, and an integer $f\ge 1$, construct a sensitivity oracle that, after preprocessing $G$, answers exactly for every set $U$ of at most $f$ edge insertions and deletions the value of $\operatorname{maxflow}_{G\oplus U}(s,t)$, equivalently $\operatorname{mincut}_{G\oplus U}(s,t)$, without recomputing the optimization problem from scratch. The goal is an efficient oracle with compact, preferably near-optimal, space usage and efficient query time, for arbitrary $f$.
title: Baswana–Bhanja–Pandey open problem on dynamic exact flow/min-cut sensitivity oracles

Kim's conjecture asserts that the motivic Chabauty--Kim loci of $X$ eventually determine exactly the $S$-integral points: there exists $n_{0}$ such that, for every depth $n\ge n_{0}$, $X^{\mathrm{CK}}_{n}(K,S)=X(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $X^{\mathrm{CK}}_{n}(K,S)$ denotes the depth-$n$ Chabauty--Kim locus.
title: Kim’s conjecture for S-integral points on the thrice-punctured line

literal: For each integer $d\geq 5$, determine the least integer $B(d)$ such that the following holds: for every homogeneous form $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ of degree $d$, let $X_F\subset\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ be the hypersurface $F=0$ and let $\sigma(F)=\dim\operatorname{Sing}(X_F)$. title: Birch’s theorem and the variable-bound problem for the smooth Hasse principle

individual_assessment: Pairwise moment constraints suggest a finite LP certificate on a chosen n, but arbitrary monotone submodular f and all marginals need a structural extremal reduction or a genuine violating instance. No such instance established; source successor unchecked.
literal: For every integer $n\ge 1$, every monotone submodular function $f:2^{[n]}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and every marginal vector $x\in[0,1]^n$ with $f^{++}(x)>0$, the correlation gap under pairwise independence is at most $4/3$: $\frac{f^{+}(x)}{f^{++}(x)}\le\frac{4}{3}$. Here $f^{+}(x)=\max\{\mathbb{E}[f(S)]:S=\{i:X_i=1\},\ X\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \mathbb{E}[X_i]=x_i\}$, while $f^{++}(x)$ is the same maximum restricted to jointly distributed random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ that are pairwise independent.
title: Pairwise independent correlation gap conjecture

literal: Let $h_1(t)=Cte^{-pi t^2}$ be the first Hermite function, where $C\neq 0$, and for $a,b>0$ define the Gabor system $\mathcal{G}(h_1,a,b)=\{e^{2\pi i mbt}h_1(t-na):m,n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$. Determine whether $\mathcal{G}(h_1,a,b)$ is a frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ exactly when $ab<1$ and $ab\neq N/(N+1)$ for every positive integer $N$. Equivalently, the conjecture asserts that the non-frame set is $\{(a,b)\in(0,\infty)^2:ab\geq 1\}\cup\{(a,b)\in(0,\infty)^2:ab=N/(N+1)\text{ for some }N\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\}$.
title: Lyubarskii–Nes conjecture on the frame set of the first Hermite function

literal: Given a weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$, where $w:E\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, find an integral cycle basis $\mathcal{B}$ minimizing its total weight $\sum_{C\in\mathcal{B}}\sum_{e\in C}w(e)$. Here an integral cycle basis is a basis of the integer cycle lattice of $G$, equivalently, a cycle basis whose cycle vectors form a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of that lattice. Determine the computational complexity of this optimization problem and characterize the graphs for which minimum cycle bases are integral for every edge-weight function.
title: Minimum forward and integral cycle basis problems

When such protocols exist, determine the required communication cost; when they do not, prove that no finite classical communication suffices.
title: Finite classical-communication simulation problem for quantum communication and Bell nonlocality

title: Optimal alphabet size for synchronization strings

literal: Let $E_n$ be the explicit family of $n$-dimensional ellipsoids considered in the cited problem, accessed through a membership oracle. Determine the quantum membership-query complexity of producing, for every $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|c\|_2=1$, a point $x$ satisfying $x\in E_n$ and $c^{\mathsf T}x\geq\max_{y\in E_n}c^{\mathsf T}y-\Theta(n^{-2})$. title: Quantum query complexity of high-accuracy convex optimization

literal:
Let $\mathbb{T}^2=\mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ be the flat unit torus, let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ be independent samples of $n$ independent points uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and let $d_{\mathbb{T}^2}$ denote the torus distance. For every finite $q\ge 1$, determine the exact leading asymptotics, including the leading constant, of
$$
C_{n,q}=\mathbb{E}\left[\min_{\sigma\in S_n}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n d_{\mathbb{T}^2}(X_i,Y_{\sigma(i)})^q\right]
$$
as $n\to\infty$. In particular, determine the exact asymptotics in the endpoint case $q=1$ for periodic matching on the flat two-dimensional torus.
title: Talagrand’s question on periodic two-dimensional random matching

individual_assessment: For every k and all N in one congruence class, regular Cayley tournament must be simultaneously vertex-critical for two invariants. A small tournament certificate or one prime order misses the quantified construction.
literal: For every integer $k\ge 3$, does there exist a positive even integer $m_k$ such that, for every integer $N>1$ satisfying $N\equiv 1\pmod{m_k}$, there is a regular, vertex-transitive Cayley tournament $T$ on $N$ vertices with $\omega(T)=\chi(T)=k$ and such that, for every vertex $v\in V(T)$, $\omega(T-v)\le k-1$ and $\chi(T-v)\le k-1$? Here $\omega(T)$ is the minimum clique number among the backedge graphs of $T$, and $\chi(T)$ is the dichromatic number.
title: Aboulker–Aubian–Charbit–Lopes conjecture on simultaneously critical Cayley tournaments

literal: For every integer $t\ge 1$ and every planar graph $H$, there exists a constant $c=c(t,H)$ such that every graph $G$ with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,t}$ and with no induced minor isomorphic to $H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tree\text{-}\alpha}(G)\le c$. Here $\operatorname{tree\text{-}\alpha}(G)=\min_{(T,\{B_x\})}\max_{x\in V(T)}\alpha(G[B_x])$, where the minimum ranges over all tree decompositions $(T,\{B_x\})$ of $G$.
title: Dallard–Krnc–Kwon–Milanič–Munaro–Štorgel–Wiederrecht path-independence conjecture
